correctness.rationale: The reflection parity blocks reduce to analytic rank-one perturbations on [-1,1]; at zero aperture each has simple isolated top eigenvalue 2(k(0)±k(2a)), strictly positive. Rayleigh perturbation gives the explicit ε³ coefficient including the off-constant-mode term, and parity under ε→−ε removes odd coefficients after normalization. The gap has nonzero W-derivative at W=nπ/(2a), so the analytic implicit function theorem proves unique crossings and the stated ε² coefficient with O(ε⁴) remainder; norm convergence excludes a third top eigenvalue. Independent Nyström quadrature and trace checks in the accompanying checker pass for 12 parameter cases. Finite tests supplement, do not prove, the analytic statement.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2011 disjoint-band spectral equivalence and 2013 eigenfunction evaluation are broader in operator setup but neither inspected statement gives the local narrow-aperture crossing asymptotic. The published detachment result quantifies loss of concentration when a segment is separated from a large interval; it does not compare two parity-sector top eigenvalues near sinc resonances.

value.rationale: Leading bandpass-prolate eigenfunctions are used to optimize Fourier concentration on two separated time windows. The known qualitative parity switching leaves the sharp location and how it depends on finite aperture undetermined. A universal positive second-order drift for each resonant mode, plus uniqueness and transversality of the double optimum, quantifies a natural bifurcation and directly informs narrow-band separation settings; it is neither a parameter substitution nor a restatement of known degeneracy.
